cause: Source defect, not a code error. In all 157 treadmill recordings (22 participants) the gcLeft ToeOff column is identical to the gcRight ToeOff column (same Header, same values) while heel strikes differ. 0 of 2,990 non-treadmill recordings have this. The shared toe-offs fall at the right belt's load offset (median -0.010 to -0.025 s); the left belt unloads about 0.4 to 0.5 s later. Left stance therefore ran from the left heel strike to the right leg's next toe-off, about 0.10 of the cycle.
evidence: docs/quality/audits/gt21-rb06-belt-evidence.json (one recording per participant: source toe-off fraction and belt-loaded fraction, both legs)
AB06 treadmill_01_01: left HS 15.63 s, shared TO 15.91 s, left belt loaded 15.625 to 16.625 s; right HS 14.795, TO 15.91, right belt loaded 14.795 to 15.87
fix: gt21_rb_segment.left_toe_off_copied_from_right(mode, gcLeft, gcRight): treadmill only, identical ToeOff arrays with at least one event. RB03 then treats left treadmill stance as unavailable: left force mask empty, step stance_samples and force_missing_stance_samples null with a stance_unavailable reason, no toe-off force check. The export gives no incomplete_stance_force flag for null stance. Nothing is rebuilt from belt load (that would be invented timing). Right leg and all other modes untouched. Export and export readback now read the *_20261126 RB03 roots.
test: tests/test_gt21_rb_segment.py: 3 new synthetic tests (the end-to-end one fails without the runner change); 43 tests pass in the segment and export test files
